title: It’s OK to “Lie” on Your Resume — If You Do It This Way
description:
Is it okay to lie on your resume?
Not exactly — but changing your job title on a resume can be the right move when done correctly.

Many companies use internal or vague job titles that don’t match what employers and recruiters search for. Translating your title to a market-recognized job title (like Project Manager, Analyst, or Coordinator) helps recruiters understand your experience in seconds.

What’s not okay?
Inflating your level, claiming skills you don’t have, or misrepresenting your experience. That will cost you interviews.

Rule of thumb:
If you can clearly explain the title change in an interview, it’s ethical and acceptable.

transcript: It's okay to lie on your resume, but not the way you think. Before anyone panics, lying about your experience, inflating your level, or claiming skills you don't have is a hard no. That will catch up with you. But here's what's okay and honestly necessary. Clarity. If your company use bag or internal job titles, you are allowed to translate that title into something employers actually understand. For example, maybe your internal title was program specialist, but you were managing timeline, stakeholders, deliverables, budgets. That's a project manager. Same work, clearer language. What's not okay is inflating your level. Analyst to director, no. Coordinator to VP, absolutely not. Here's the rules I give clients. If you can explain the title change confidently in an interview, that's fair. It's not lying. It's just making your experience visible. Follow me at Kersner Careers for more hot job tips.
